comparison_policy: Rated continuous, peak transient, model estimate, measured prototype and vendor-reported peak are distinct metric kinds.
Unknown or unmatched denominator, duty, thermal, bus or load boundaries are NOT_COMPARABLE.
Every candidate includes the complete installed mass and energy boundary.
J1 leg actuator, J2 wrist and J3 tendon hand are separate leaderboards.

claim_ceiling: The source figures are paper/vendor references, not Luminous reproductions. Missing boundaries remain NOT_COMPARABLE.
source_addendum: Hu et al. add a parallel 3-PRS/SS origami wrist architecture; currently qualitative only because a complete numeric matched boundary was not established.
The sensorized tendon continuum reference uses redundant tension transducers, encoders and IMUs in addition to tendon resistance sensing; it is not a sensorless or load-bearing-joint qualification.
The printed TPU musculoskeletal leg demonstrates coordinated motion under external suspension and partial body-weight support, not unsupported full-body locomotion.
Self-healing DEA figures are material/lab-actuator results under high electric field and thermal repair conditions, not a qualified joint result.

J1 prediction error is concentrated after release: the design model underpredicts push-off phase duration and push-off rise but overpredicts total rise by 16.6%; measured motor parameters and mass explain 11.3 percentage points, leaving 5.3 for transmission, guide and control effects. The nominal 52 N*m 2x command slightly exceeds the tabulated 51.5 N*m peak, so command, rating and actual measured joint torque must remain distinct.

Unitree GO-M8010-6 provides a more concrete commercial motor reference than H1 peak density alone: approx 0.530 kg and 23.7 N*m maximum torque; 44.72 N*m/kg is calculated maximum torque divided by approximate listed mass and is not continuous rated density.

Lai et al. 2026 report a high-k self-healing PABTU bilayer DEA with visible deformation at 30 V and >130% area strain at 120 V; complete joint work, fatigue and healed recovery remain to be established from the full article.
Corrected from arXiv:2609.22795v1 Table I: seven slot-pole families, including 27S/30P; diameter <=98 mm and axial length <=50 mm package constraints; winding factor k_w,1 >0.9.

The paper reports seven slot-pole-specific standardized quadratic ridge motor surrogates, each trained on 1000 valid LHS designs from an eight-dimensional cross-sectional design space and checked against 200 independent validation cases. Reported R2 0.9681–0.9993 applies to representative 18S/20P outputs only.
The source uses constrained NSGA-II with population 48 for 30 generations and an inner L-BFGS-B over twelve Bezier torque-profile variables. These methods are transcribed, not reproduced.

Add cross-layer whole-robot references separately from joint torque-density comparators: PACE reports 32% lower ANYmal full COT (reported value 1.27) across three primary and ten additional platforms; RAIBO2 reports marathon completion in 4 h 19 min 52 s with COT 0.25.

Kang et al. 2026 provides a high-ratio friction transfer comparator: Stribeck extension lowers identification error by 16% and reduces mean-velocity sim-to-real degradation at 0.3 and 1.0 m/s command levels.
